questions.q: What number should the SR-5 abstract lead with, and why?
options: The gross Sharpe of 0.76, because it's the strategy's full potential
The net Sharpe of 0.42, because leading with the bigger gross number lets a reader anchor on a figure that doesn't survive real costs
The maximum single-day return, because it's the most memorable
The capacity estimate, because it matters most to a PM
questions.explain: The abstract should lead with the net Sharpe of 0.42 rather than the gross 0.76, so a reader can't anchor on a number that doesn't reflect real trading costs.

questions.q: What are the three readers a performance report is written for?
options: The compliance team, the marketing team, and the CEO
A portfolio manager, a risk manager, and future you trying to reproduce the result
The data vendor, the exchange, and the regulator
Only the person who built the strategy
questions.explain: A performance report serves a PM deciding on allocation, a risk manager checking fit against the book, and a future reader (often yourself) who needs to reproduce or revisit the work.

questions.q: Why should a results table always show gross and net numbers side by side instead of one blended figure?
options: Regulators require two columns in every report
A single blended number hides how much of the edge survives real transaction costs, which is the most decision-relevant comparison
It makes the table visually symmetrical
Gross and net numbers must always be identical, so showing both is a consistency check
questions.explain: Showing gross and net side by side (e.g., Sharpe 0.76 gross vs. 0.42 net) keeps the cost impact visible rather than letting one blended number obscure it.

questions.q: Which of these is a genuine limitation of SR-5 that the report should state plainly?
options: The strategy has never been backtested on any data
The sample period includes only one true panic (COVID), so tail behavior rests on thin evidence, and capacity is capped around $150M before net Sharpe erodes below 0.2
The strategy's Sharpe ratio is undefined
The point-in-time universe has no effect on early-period results
questions.explain: Genuine limitations include the thin sample of true panics, the growing point-in-time universe (9 to 11 names), and the ~$150M capacity ceiling from Lesson 11.

questions.q: What is the standard structure of a systematic-strategy performance report, in order?
options: Results, abstract, appendix, limitations
Abstract, data & methodology, results, risk analysis, limitations, appendix
Limitations, risk analysis, results, abstract
Appendix, abstract, methodology, results
questions.explain: The standard order is abstract, data and methodology, results, risk analysis, limitations, then appendix — a predictable shape that lets different readers find what they need.
